note: title and implication are IGNIS wording (assistant-written paraphrase of scope); the source's own words are in the linked assertion. briefRole: 'finding' items lead a safety-area section, 'context' items explain relevance and are never presented as measurements.

records.title: Spacecraft-scale fires reached a steady size; the vehicle mattered more than expected
records.implication: In NASA's first three Saffire burns, flames spread quickly to a steady size and burn rate, and the size of the spacecraft affected the fire more than anticipated. Treat the surrounding vehicle as part of the fire problem, not just the material.

domain.description: Uncrewed Cygnus vehicles after ISS departure; materials and flows not stated in this summary.

records.title: Reducing pressure slowed flame spread in Saffire results
records.implication: NASA reports that Saffire flame-spread results show reducing pressure slows spread. This is a direction, not a magnitude, and pressure was not the only condition that differed between flights; it does not make a lower-pressure, oxygen-enriched cabin safe.

domain.description: Family-level statement about Saffire results; the flights, materials, oxygen levels and pressures behind it are in references the page cites (not acquired).

records.title: In spacecraft-scale burns, gases—not heat—were the larger hazard
records.implication: Saffire IV–VI fires of 1.5–3.2 kW raised temperature significantly only near the fire, while CO and CO2 rose enough in the PMMA tests to exceed the 1-hour CO2 and 24-hour CO limits. The authors state these results still need extending to partial gravity.

domain.description: Saffire IV-1, V-2 and VI-2/3/4 burns (S-CAL Table 1): SIBAL, cotton and PMMA samples, concurrent flow, ambient pressures 100.0, 70.7, 54.1 and 54.6 kPa as printed; free air volumes 17-19 m³.

records.title: Why oxygen-enriched, lower-pressure atmospheres matter
records.implication: The challenge states that the planned Moon Base and rovers are expected to use increased oxygen at reduced pressure, and that flammability depends strongly on oxygen and air flow. This is a planning expectation, not an IGNIS recommendation or a tested habitat atmosphere.

records.title: Microgravity smoke particles were not significantly different from normal-gravity ones
records.implication: In SAME, smoke from heated spacecraft materials varied in shape and average diameter, but was not significantly different from smoke made in equivalent normal-gravity experiments. This concerns smoke from heated (pyrolysing) samples, not every fire.

domain.description: Oxidative pyrolysis of five spacecraft materials on the ISS, with controlled heating temperature, air flow and aging (abstract).

records.title: Two spacecraft smoke detectors did not detect every smoke type
records.implication: The two spacecraft smoke detectors tested in SAME missed some smoke types, so the authors conclude next-generation detectors must be tested against smoke from relevant space materials. The abstract does not say which detector missed which smoke.

exclusions: Alarm thresholds or delays (not reported in the abstract)

records.title: A typical alarm threshold was reached only after most hazardous gas had been released
records.implication: The cited Saffire passage reports smoke detection by ionization and light scattering, with a typical threshold reached at a reported time of 981 s after most hazardous gas release. The sentence does not specify the event, threshold value or clock origin. Treat 981 s as a source-specific reported clock value; it does not establish a detector delay or a comparison with other Saffire alarm times.

domain.description: One Saffire fire event in an uncrewed Cygnus; the event, threshold value and clock origin are not given in the sentence.

records.title: A droplet flame can look extinguished while it keeps burning as a cool flame
records.implication: FLEX observed hot-flame extinction leading to low-temperature 'cool-flame' burning; these cool flames produce partially oxidized fuel and can potentially re-ignite to hot flames. Visible-flame disappearance is not proof that all reaction has stopped—at least for the tested liquid-fuel droplets.

domain.description: Isolated n-alkane fuel droplets (for example heptane, decane) in the FLEX chamber.

records.title: Methanol droplets showed diffusive and radiative extinction across separately stated O2, CO2 and helium ranges
records.implication: FLEX methanol-droplet tests covered 13–30% O2, 5–75% CO2 and 5–45% He (separate ranges), and showed extinction by water absorption and by radiation. The ranges are not a tested grid of every combination, and droplet results do not set a cabin suppressant dose.

domain.description: Methanol droplets, initial diameter 1-4.5 mm; O2, CO2 and He ranges stated separately on the slide.

records.title: The Saffire VI cabin model receives the fire as a prescribed source
records.implication: In the published Saffire VI transport model, the mass generation rate and heat addition rate are applied at the flow-unit outlet. The model transports a given fire's heat and products; it does not predict the burning itself.

domain.description: Saffire VI events 5, 6 and 8 in an uncrewed Cygnus, about 54-55 kPa and 29-31% O2 as printed.

records.title: Saffire VI model curves were shifted to match each sensor's initial value
records.implication: The initial cabin CO2 was set from the sensors' mean, and the model curves were then raised or lowered to match each sensor's initial value (events 5, 6 and 8). Initial agreement is imposed; later change remains a useful conditional comparison.

domain.description: Saffire VI events 5, 6 and 8, remote sensors RS1-RS6.

records.title: SIBAL burn: close CO2 totals, but the rise was underpredicted
records.implication: For the Saffire VI SIBAL burn, the CO2 added by the model source and the remote-inferred rise were close, and the authors say steady-state agreement is expected from that; they also report the rise is underpredicted at all locations.

domain.description: Saffire VI event 5: SIBAL fabric, 31.0% O2 at 54.1 kPa, concurrent flow.

records.title: Two-sided PMMA burn: source and remote CO2 totals closely match
records.implication: For the Saffire VI two-sided PMMA burn, the remote-inferred CO2 increase and the model's total source input closely match. A close integrated total is not evidence of accurate transient behaviour.

domain.description: Saffire VI event 6: two-sided PMMA, 30.3% O2 at 54.6 kPa, concurrent flow.

records.title: Model heat input for the PMMA burn is sensible heat added to the cabin
records.implication: Integrating the heat addition rate for the Saffire VI two-sided PMMA burn gives 497 kJ of heat added to the cabin. This is sensible heat delivered by the flow unit, a different quantity from the fire's chemical heat release.

records.title: Calorimetry total heat release for the two-sided PMMA burn
records.implication: Oxygen-consumption calorimetry gives a total heat release of 1280 kJ for the two-sided PMMA sample (Saffire VI, 780 s burn). It measures the fire's chemical heat release at the sample, not heat delivered to the cabin.

domain.description: S-CAL VI-3 (two-sided PMMA), matched to S-VI event 6 by material and configuration.

records.title: Saffire V model source was scaled to the remote-sensor CO2 total
records.implication: For Saffire V event 6, the source curve built from the RS3 outlet sensor gave 29.9 g CO2, while the six remote sensors implied 54.4 g; the source was scaled by 1.82 to match. Agreement in the total CO2 is therefore built in, not predicted.
